claim.why_it_matters: A reader of the transcription sees the exception list cut off at 'rules 2 through' and a stray '5.' item, so the scope of the qualification exceptions (rules 2 through 5) is not stated in one place and the text looks like a sixth-rule sub-list.
claim.pdf_says: uniqueness shall then be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced, except as specified in rules 2 through 5.  All available qualifiers need not be specified so long as uniqueness is established.
claim.markdown_says:
uniqueness shall then be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced, except as specified in rules 2 through

   5\. All available qualifiers need not be specified so long as uniqueness is established.
claim.explanation: The printed line break inside the sentence 'except as specified in rules 2 through 5.' was turned into a paragraph break, so the cross-reference reads 'rules 2 through' (incomplete) and the remainder starts a new paragraph beginning '5\.', which renders as if it were a list item numbered 5 inside rule 6. The sentence should be one paragraph ending '...rules 2 through 5. All available qualifiers...'.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 83 (PDF p105), 8.4.1.1 rule 6 continuation paragraph: the line wraps after 'rules 2 through' and the next line begins '5.  All available qualifiers...'. The markdown (page-105.md lines 31-33) holds every word in the same order: '...except as specified in rules 2 through' then a blank line, then '5\. All available qualifiers need not be specified...'. Nothing is missing, misplaced or reworded. The only difference is that a printed line wrap became a paragraph break. The period after 5 is backslash-escaped, so Markdown does not render it as an ordered-list item, and a reader still sees 'rules 2 through ... 5.'. This is a line-wrapping and formatting artifact that does not change the content or the meaning of the exception range (rules 2 through 5). The claim also calls it 'misplaced-content', which it is not. A cosmetic join of the two lines would tidy it, but it is not a genuine content discrepancy.
